The blind and pallid undercraw digs its own tunnels a dozen 
feet below the bogs of the Fenlands. Thick questing antenna 
sniff out rotten root to munch on in the damp and fertile black 
soil. Occasionally the crustacean will dig too deep and fall into 
the drier expanse of the stone-carved Umbrawells and have to 
contend with the denizens that call those dark halls home
Undercraw
Length - 10 in.
Gorr Hatchling
Length - 1 ft. 8 in.
Curious to a fault, the gorr hatchlings venture from their nest to sniff out new food whenever their adult kin look the other way. While 
their scales offer a measure of safety from the many dangers of the Umbrawells, too many predators are happy to snatch a wayward 
gorr from its home, causing only the most wary to survive into adulthood.
Often only seen as an unremarkable stony nub, the mollucite juvenile is usually passed by predators countless times, thinking it is 
nothing more than another stone outcropping. Th is subterranean mollusk, with its slow metabolism, remains in this small state for 
decades before slowing growing into its adult form, only if it is successful in catching sizable prey.
Th ousands of glossy shells reflect the light of the bioluminescent fungi that the swarm consumes in their perpetual need to grow. 
While this shifting mass of larvae moves slowly across surfaces, they do so with an inexorable pace, swarming around inedible 
obstacles and ripping apart anything they can't eat. Th eir parents tend to them, expelling vast piles of mulch for them to feast upon.
Small grimy maggot-like bodies squirm in the abyssal crevices that riddle the Umbrawells. Many of these cramped cracks host a 
myriad of blind bottom dwelling detritus scavengers, perfect prey for the young acrynn grub to clasp onto and attack. Feasting and 
growing in the dark until they moult into their larger stalking adult forms.
